answer: A nectar pool is guarded by a pigment-marked, non-poolable bond. Each applicant locks one bond with a pigment tag, recorded against a timber record of verified tasks. Auditors check bond and record; a failed check burns the bond and slashes linked bonds in its cluster. The k-th fake costs 25 plus 0.09k squared units, rising with n; a burned pigment bond cannot be reissued, auditors enforce bond and cluster forfeiture. One fake costs 25.09 units; 1,000 cost 30,070,015. A rented-history ring fails, as shared pigment trails trigger slashing, while an honest agent pays once.
